bullets.title: Stories of Your Life and Others
bullets.note:
This collection of short stories by Ted Chiang is incredible. Despite the fact
that Ted isn’t a full-time science fiction writer, he is the equivalent of
Scorcese or Wayne Gretzky in that world -- he has won four Hugo, four Nebula,
and four Locus Awards, among others. The recent hit film
[Arrival](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=diK&mc=1&s=bomwH&u=w&y=5&)
(94% on Rotten Tomatoes), one of my favorite movies of the last 3-5 years and
starring Amy Adams and Jeremy Renner, is based on one of Ted’s short stories.
Gizmodo has written that “The arrival of a new piece of short fiction by Ted
Chiang is always cause for celebration and parades and wild dancing.” Read the
first few stories and you’ll know why.

bullets.title: Karma
bullets.note:
From the creators of Set. This fits in a pocket and can be played in 5-15
minutes. I enjoy alternating this with the [Monopoly
DEAL](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=diA&mc=1&s=bomwH&u=w&y=p&)
card game I mentioned last week. Both games can be played with two players and
pair well with Merlot or Pinot noir.

bullets.title: “Man Who Studied 1,000 Deaths to Learn How to Live”
bullets.note:
from my podcast, BJ Miller, MD? [This is the most beautiful and powerful
article about
him](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=di8&mc=1&s=bomwH&u=w&y=f&)
that I’ve ever read, courtesy of NYT Magazine. Take the time to [read
it](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=di8&mc=1&s=bomwH&u=w&y=f&).
It might change your life. At the very least, it will make you feel emotions
you probably need to feel.

bullets.title: Kubo and the Two Strings
bullets.note:
This was originally (and strongly) recommended to me by Kevin Rose in his
once-monthly [The
Journal](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=diC&mc=1&s=bomwH&u=w&y=X&)
newsletter. It’s beautiful. I almost bawled several times -- on a plane, no
less -- but perhaps I’m just a Japanophile who does too many drugs. You
decide. Here’s the basic premise: A young boy named Kubo must locate a magical
suit of armor worn by his late father in order to defeat a vengeful spirit
from the past.
